# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_014_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 6

**1** In the middle of the plain she pointed out a great white rock to me, and cut into the rock was a doorway — more brilliant than the sun. Its brightness amazed me. **2** Twelve virgins were standing around the doorway. The four stationed at its corners seemed the most glorious of all, but all twelve were radiant. **3** Outside the doorway stood two young men. Between them I could see four more young men, more glorious in appearance, wearing dark clothing, their shoulders bare, their hair loose — they looked sad. **4** The six builders gave these young men instructions to bring stones for the tower. They hauled stones from the plain and from a nearby lake. **5** The stones from the plain were already prepared — cut and ready. They were fitted into the tower as they arrived, stacked one on another so seamlessly you couldn't find the joints. **6** The stones from the lake, once placed in the wall, turned transparent — glassy, shining, brilliant. They lit up the whole building. **7** I noticed the old woman was no longer present. After a moment I looked again, and coming toward me was a young woman in bridal dress — wearing dark sandals and a garland of asphodel. **8** "Are you real? Are you in glory?" I asked. "Who are you?" She said, "I am the Church." "But you're so young," I said. "Aren't you the old woman I've been seeing?" She answered simply: "I am the same person."

---

*PNEUMA note: The revelation "I am the same" is one of the Shepherd's most theologically charged moments. The Church's aging to youth signals her spiritual renewal — she grows younger as her members repent.*
